data.title: Historical Timeline: Ordering the events of a school day

challenges.title: Morning Routine History
challenges.instruction: Put these morning events in the order they happened in history, from oldest to newest.

events.label: Mechanical Alarm Clock
events.description: The first mechanical alarm clock that could ring at a set time was invented around 1500.

events.label: Glass Toothbrush
events.description: The modern toothbrush with bristles and a glass handle was mass-produced around 1780.

events.label: Instant Breakfast Cereal
events.description: Flaked breakfast cereals were first packaged and sold to families in 1894.

events.label: Electric Hair Dryer
events.description: The first handheld electric hair dryer for home use appeared around 1920.

events.label: Digital Coffee Maker
events.description: The first programmable automatic drip coffee makers came to kitchens in 1975.

challenges.hint: Think about which morning habits people invented first long ago.
challenges.narration: Let's explore how our morning routines changed over time!

challenges.title: Getting to School
challenges.instruction: Put these ways of traveling to school in the order they were invented, from oldest to newest.

events.label: Horse-Drawn Omnibus
events.description: Horse-drawn carriages began carrying children and citizens around towns in the 1820s.

events.label: The Safety Bicycle
events.description: The modern bicycle with two equal-sized wheels became popular for riding around 1885.

events.label: Yellow School Bus
events.description: The standard yellow motor-powered school bus was introduced for students in 1939.

events.label: Subway System Ride
events.description: Electric urban underground trains became a daily commute option for kids in the 1950s.

events.label: Electric Scooter
events.description: Modern battery-powered stand-up scooters became a popular way to cruise to school by 2018.

challenges.hint: Think about whether children rode horses or cars to school first.
challenges.narration: Let's travel through time to see how students got to their classrooms!

challenges.title: Classroom Tools
challenges.instruction: Put these school supply inventions in the order they were created, from oldest to newest.

events.label: Wooden Slate Pencil
events.description: Students used small stone slate boards and slate pencils for writing practice in the 1780s.

events.label: Rubber Eraser
events.description: Rubbers made from natural rubber to wipe away pencil marks were sold starting in 1770.

events.label: Colored Crayons
events.description: The first boxes of safe, colorful wax crayons for school children were made in 1903.

events.label: Ballpoint Pen
events.description: Modern ballpoint pens that did not spill ink everywhere became widely used in the 1940s.

events.label: Interactive Whiteboard
events.description: Large touch-sensitive digital screens began replacing chalkboards in classrooms in 1991.

challenges.hint: Consider which tools students used in old-fashioned one-room schoolhouses.
challenges.narration: Let's discover when your favorite school supplies were first invented!

challenges.title: Recess and Playtime
challenges.instruction: Put these recess games and playground items in the order they were invented, from oldest to newest.

events.label: Playground Jungle Gym
events.description: The first metal climbing frame for schoolyards was patented in the early 1920s.

events.label: Rubber Playground Ball
events.description: Bouncy red rubber kickballs used for games at recess were invented in the 1930s.

events.label: The Hula Hoop
events.description: Plastic hula hoops became a massive playground craze across schools in 1958.

events.label: The Skateboard
events.description: Roller skate wheels attached to wooden boards turned into popular toys in the 1960s.

events.label: Handheld Digital Pet
events.description: Small digital egg-shaped toys that kids fed and cared for at recess launched in 1996.

challenges.hint: Think about which games kids played on the playground long before video games.
challenges.narration: Let's find out when children started playing with these classic recess items!
